name: Primer tan / base tan

image.caption: Aerial view of Tan Son Nhut Air Base (Vietnam) in June 1968

lead: A primer or base tan is a tan built up before a trip or sun-heavy period, so you arrive already bronzed and, people hope, burn less. It is often gained through gradual sun exposure or tanning beds.

The chain is biological: UVB damages skin-cell DNA and triggers melanin production, which absorbs some UV. A UVB-induced tan has been described as giving modest protection, roughly SPF 3, meaning tanned skin tolerates up to about three times the exposure of pale skin. The tan itself arises from UV-induced DNA damage, and UVA darkening of existing melanin gives quick colour but no real protection.

paras: People expose skin in short, gradual sessions in the weeks before a trip, in the sun or on sunbeds, then continue sun care on holiday. The tan is visible within days of exposure.

UV exposure causes sunburn and is linked to skin cancer and ageing. Tanning devices are classified as carcinogenic to humans, and in two US surveys 58% of indoor tanners reported burns during sessions.

angle.text: You build a primer or base tan before a trip so you arrive already bronzed and, you hope, burn less. The tan is the visible result of UV triggering melanin production. The protection it gives has been measured as modest, around SPF 3.

lead: A primer tan or base tan is a tan acquired before a holiday or sun-heavy period, in the belief that it will protect the skin from later sunburn. It is commonly gained through gradual sun exposure or tanning bed sessions [1][2].

A UVB-induced tan does offer modest protection, roughly an SPF of about 3 according to one summary, meaning tanned skin tolerates up to about three times the exposure of pale skin [1]. The tan itself, however, arises from UV-induced DNA damage [1]. Surveys of young people have found that beliefs in 'safe tanning' persist [3].
Public health sources report that indoor tanning raises melanoma risk, and in two US surveys 58% of indoor tanners reported burns during sessions [2].
infobox: About SPF 3 for a UVB-induced tan [1]

paras: Proponents say a base tan prepares skin for intense sun, and that tanning bed sessions give controlled, predictable exposure for building one [2]. The idea is widely held in the general public, not only in looksmaxxing circles.

UVA oxidizes existing melanin, causing a quick darkening that fades and adds no real protection, while UVB damages DNA and triggers new melanin production, producing a longer-lasting tan after two or three days [1]. Dark skin offers some protection but does not prevent photoageing or melanoma [1].

Survey research rather than trials has examined this belief. A survey of 909 21-year-old New Zealanders found that knowledge of melanoma was high but myths about 'safe tanning' persisted [3]. A review in Clinics in Dermatology has examined health claims advertised for indoor tanning [4], and a nursing journal article has asked whether a base tan protects or gives a false sense of security [5]. IARC classified tanning devices as carcinogenic to humans in 2009, and a 2014 meta-analysis found 16% higher melanoma risk among indoor tanners [2].

In 2016 the FTC settled with a tanning bed marketer over claims including that tanning was needed for vitamin D, with refunds of $5.3 million [2]. The US FDA reclassified tanning beds as moderate risk in 2014 and requires a warning against use by under-18s [2].
